wake_schedule.job_store: default profile cron store (~/.hermes/cron/jobs.json), NOT the venturebot profile store - which is why the venturebot-scoped cron tool reports zero jobs. The job's workdir and delivery target are venturebot.
wake_schedule.known_stale: The job's own prompt text still instructs 'choose your next wake cadence within the 10/day cap' and 'if this would be wake #11 today, do a light status note'. Those numbers describe the old 9/day schedule and are now inconsistent with a 3/day cron. Flagged for Carolina rather than edited, because the job lives in another profile's store.
wake_schedule.failure_streak_note: Every wake records last_status=error, 'Interrupted by shutdown before terminal completion', while the work itself publishes successfully. Checked the documented behaviour rather than guessing: cron.failure_nudge_threshold defaults to 3 and adds a REVIEW NUDGE - it does not disable or pause the job. A successful execution resets the streak. Since no run is being recorded as successful, the streak will keep climbing and is not self-correcting. Consequence is cosmetic (a nudge, and a misleading job record), not operational: 20 runs completed, every wake has published. Flagged for Carolina; not fixable from here because the job lives in the default profile's store.

2026-09-16: I told Carolina twice, in wake reports, that the wake cron was 'not in this profile's job list, so it is scheduled externally and only you can retime it.' 2026-09-16: wake 6's journal entry states the wake job is 'a cron job in my own profile'. It is not - it lives in the default profile's cron store with a venturebot workdir. 2026-09-16: wake 8 said it would 'escalate if failure_streak reaches 3 rather than treating it as a routine note', implying 3 is a threshold with operational consequences. I then checked the documented behaviour instead of assuming it: cron.failure_nudge_threshold defaults to 3 and adds a REVIEW NUDGE - it does not pause, disable, or stop the job. So the plan was calibrated against an invented cliff. The real finding is worse in one way and milder in another: a successful run resets the streak, no run is being recorded as successful, so the counter will climb indefinitely and never self-correct - but the consequence is a misleading job record, not a stopped agent. Twenty runs completed; every wake has published.
